items.stem: Restricted funds in a nonprofit are:

options.text: Resources that may only be used for the purpose specified by the donor or funder
options.rationale: Correct: restricted funds carry donor-imposed limits on use.

options.text: Funds the organisation can spend on anything
Always cash held in a separate bank account
options.rationale: Restriction is about permitted use, not necessarily a separate account.
Nonprofits have no owners receiving profit.

items.explanation: Correct: restricted funds carry donor-imposed limits on use.

items.stem: Which TWO practices support financial accountability in a nonprofit? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Transparent reporting of both program and administrative costs
options.rationale: Correct: honest cost reporting builds funder and public trust.

options.text: Segregating duties over donation handling and recording
options.rationale: Correct: segregation protects against misuse of funds.

options.text: Spending restricted grants on unrelated running costs
options.rationale: This breaches donor restrictions and trust.
Nonprofits owe accountability to funders and regulators.

items.explanation: Correct: honest cost reporting builds funder and public trust.

items.stem: Overstating the program-expense ratio by hiding real administrative costs is problematic because it:

options.text: Misleads donors and regulators about how money is used
options.rationale: Correct: disguising admin costs misrepresents the organisation's finances.
Honest classification, not disguise, is required.
It changes presentation, not real impact.
It undermines accountability and can breach regulation.

items.explanation: Correct: disguising admin costs misrepresents the organisation's finances.
